name: arc-diagonal-periodic-fill
description: Use when an ARC grid has sparse diagonal color marks and appears to encode a periodic diagonal tiling. Infer the period and fill the grid by diagonal residue.
---

# ARC: periodic diagonal fill

## Trigger
Use for ARC-style grids where nonzero cells appear as stripes parallel to a diagonal (often main diagonal / anti-diagonal), with zeros elsewhere, and a demo output fills the whole board in a repeating pattern.

## Rule
The filled color is constant on diagonals of slope +1: cells with the same `d = column - row` share a color. The sequence of diagonal colors repeats with a period `p`, so the output color at `(r,c)` is `color[(c-r) mod p]`.

Sparse input cells identify the color for one or more diagonal residues. Use the known dimension and all input marks to infer the period and residue-to-color mapping. Values in the same residue class should agree; conflicting assignments mean the period is wrong or the orientation/indexing needs checking.

## Procedure
1. Inspect an example output, if available. Check whether output colors are constant along diagonals and whether a short sequence repeats across rows/columns.
2. In the input, list nonzero `(r,c,color)` marks (zero-based indices) and compute `d = c-r`.
3. Find a plausible smallest period `p` such that marked cells whose `d` values are congruent modulo `p` have the same color. If outputs are available, verify this against their observed diagonal sequence; input-only empty residues can be ambiguous, so use demo requests when uncertainty is material and request cost permits.
4. Build `color_by_residue[d mod p]` from the marks. Confirm every residue needed by the output is assigned. Cross-check by placing the known marks back into the predicted tiling.
5. Fill every cell with `color_by_residue[(c-r) mod p]`; return exactly the original height and width.
6. Verify a few known marks and row-to-row shifts. Increasing `r` by one shifts the diagonal residue by `-1`; increasing `c` by one shifts it by `+1`.

## Pitfalls
- Do not fill only the visible stripes: the transformation expands the diagonal pattern over the entire grid.
- The diagonal index is `c-r`, not `r+c`; distinguish slope +1 stripes from anti-diagonal stripes.
- Residue order matters. A reversed sequence can look periodic but will fail to preserve given marks.
- Include negative diagonal indices using modulo arithmetic (e.g. Python `%` with positive `p` yields residues `0..p-1`).
- Do not infer period merely from the first couple of marked stripes; seek consistency across all marks and use demonstrations when multiple periods remain plausible.

## Verified pattern instances
- A 17x17 example had period 6 with residues `0..5` mapped to `[9,4,3,6,8,5]`; output was generated as `mapping[(c-r) % 6]`.
- A 17x17 demo showed period 3 with `[6,7,3]` by residue; a 16x16 demo showed a 7-color diagonal sequence. These examples support the general diagonal-period rule, not fixed colors or fixed periods.
